title: Contextual recall guidance can overfire during procedural state-surface work
wanted_capability: The rendered contextual-recall guidance should distinguish durable-knowledge questions from procedural work that is already operating on the right live state surface. When a task is explicitly filing gap notes, deduping gaps, opening threads, or committing repo-owned gap files, the guidance should not pressure an extra bbox_knowledge call unless a specific prior convention/runbook could materially change the operation.
missing_primitive: clear exception/decision rule in contextual-recall rendered guidance for procedural gap/thread tasks
fallback_used: Used bbox_gaps and bbox_thread as the authoritative live state surfaces, and treated the extra bbox_knowledge recall check as optional/noisy in hindsight.
notes: During a harness/tool shakedown, the agent interpreted the contextual-recall reminder as a nudge to call bbox_knowledge while already doing procedural gap/thread work. The call did not materially change the operation and emitted a large system-memory sidecar, reinforcing the separate bbox_knowledge output-spill gap. The guidance says bbox_knowledge is not the surface for active threads, but the task shape boundary remains easy to misread.
resolution_note: Addressed on branch codex/harness-tool-surface-shakedown. Rendered contextual-recall guidance now explicitly exempts procedural work already operating on authoritative live state surfaces such as bbox_gaps/bbox_gap*, bbox_thread*, notes/inbox, and repo-owned state file commits unless a specific durable convention/decision/runbook could materially change the operation.
